author: developeruche
content:
Hey <@976542403269910539>  want drop an update on the current state of `zilkworm-stateless`, the [zilkworm stateless](https://github.com/eth-act/zilkworm-stateless) guest program makes use of the [erigon's zilkworm] as a lib to handle it's state transition function. This guest program also adheres to this [spec](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/tree/projects/zkevm) and it test pipeline guidelines. 

In light of the [guest handbook document](https://github.com/eth-act/zkevm-standards/blob/main/handbooks/guest-handbook.md) from the `zkevm-standard`, some changes had to be introduced to make `zilkworm stateless` guest program conforms to the "Guest program Rubric", here are the points this rubric hilghlight;
- [x] Must implement the EEST specs and [pass all tests](https://eth-act.github.io/eest-execution-witness-dashboard/#/group/tests-zkevm%20v0.6.2).
- [x] The ELF must comply with the defined [standards](https://github.com/eth-act/zkevm-standards/tree/main/standards).
- [x] The ELF and Verification Key must be released as a signed asset in the guest program public repository releases, generated by a public, fully open-source CI pipeline.
- [x] Regarding ELF generation:
  - Modified/Custom compiler: Formal verification (FV) requirements will apply to the compiled ELF (TBD by the EF FV project team).
  - No Compiler (e.g., raw assembly/manual bytecode): The raw ELF artefact will be subject to a higher degree of formal verification scrutiny (TBD by the EF FV project team).
- [ ] The repository license must be MIT + Apache 2.0: This is currently just Apache 2.0, a discussion with the authors of [erigon's zilkworm] needs to be held first to see how MIT could be included.
- [ ] The team maintaining the guest program must be considered _sustainable_. While this is hard to define precisely, preference is given to guest programs maintained by established execution-layer teams or credible working groups.

author: developeruche
content: Regarding the last highlight, the best solution in my opinion is to have it the way other client team do where the client team also maintain the guest program and published the ELF files for the various zkVMs. <@976542403269910539>  would Erigon consider a accepting a transfer of ownership of this guest program (it would be nice to note that this would be the first non-Rust based spec compliant guest program and it is important for guest program diversification).
